_doc: Solana Security Standard (SOL-0XX) per-rule metadata — by Jelleo. HAND-AUTHORED source (like hacks/hacks.json); one entry per rule, keyed by SOL id. Merged into cli/rules.json (sync-rules.js -> scanner), semgrep metadata (sync-semgrep.js), and content/rules/*.md (sync-content.js). NOT raw-fetched by consumers (not in CHECKSUMS.txt). ADVISORY ONLY: never changes whether a rule fires, nor Semgrep `severity` / SARIF `level` (both stay WARNING). tier: high|low (submission-floor for --min-tier; LOW=hygiene/defense-in-depth/operational). Tier is a NOISE FLOOR, not a claim of un-exploitability — `--min-tier high` is for cutting alert fatigue, never the only scan for an audit; calibrate real impact via severity + SEVERITY.md. severity: high|medium|low (BASELINE impact IF a true positive; calibrate per SEVERITY.md, preconditions x access, take the lower). reachability: the first reachable call-site the reporter cites to confirm exploitability. exclusions: numbered 'do NOT flag when…' clauses — each names a SPECIFIC safe construct (never a vague 'looks fine'); the scanner still fires (fail-open), exclusions are guidance a reviewer cites by number when dismissing a finding.

SOL-001.reachability: the instruction handler that accepts now_slot (or any caller-supplied slot/timestamp) from instruction data
exclusions: the caller-supplied slot/timestamp is authenticated against Clock::get()?.slot (e.g. clamped/rejected) before any use
the value is provably discarded — never written to an account, emitted in an event, or used in a later gate (a positive 'not persisted' proof, not merely 'this handler does not seem to use it')

the handler is gated to an admin that must SIGN AND is bound by an explicit constraint to a hardcoded / program-stored admin key (constraint = signer.key() == config.admin, or has_one = admin WHERE admin is declared Signer<>) — a bare Signer<> with no such binding is a user-supplied key the caller self-assigns and is NOT sufficient, nor is a key-equality/has_one check on a non-signer account — AND the value is never re-read by a permissionless crank or downstream instruction

SOL-002.reachability: the write site that updates the shared/cross-market counter from a single market's context
exclusions: every write to the counter is gated by the market's authority proven via a SIGNATURE — a Signer<> on that authority, a PDA-signed CPI WHERE the signing PDA is derived from seeds sourced from the market account's own on-chain state (its key or a field loaded from it — NOT a caller-supplied market id from instruction data) that bind it to THIS specific market, or has_one/constraint WHERE the bound authority account is itself declared Signer<>; a has_one (or key-equality) on a NON-signing account only checks the key (not consent), and a global/unscoped authority PDA that can sign for ANY market, are NOT sufficient
the counter is strictly per-market (not a shared aggregate) and has no cross-market read path

SOL-003.reachability: the wrapper function that re-implements engine logic instead of delegating to the engine
exclusions: the wrapper delegates to the engine (CPI or shared module) and only marshals accounts

the duplicated logic is generated from / shares the engine's exact code path AND is covered by a differential test that proves wrapper(x) == engine(x) over the relevant input range (a single happy-path smoke test is NOT sufficient)

SOL-004.reachability: the risk/margin/health computation that omits a spec-mandated term
exclusions: every spec-mandated term is present (cross-checked against the protocol spec, with the specific spec clause cited by section/line — NOT a self-attested 'I checked')

the omitted term is documented in the protocol spec as zero or inapplicable for this instrument, with the spec clause cited — NOT an unverified 'by construction' assumption (that is the under-collateralization trap)

SOL-005.reachability: the realloc() call site, and whether owner / size-bound / rent-exemption are checked first
exclusions: account.owner == program_id is checked before the realloc
the new size is bounded by a validated cap AND rent-exemption is re-funded after the resize

the account is newly allocated in THIS instruction AND its size is verified == 0 before the realloc (size==0 is mandatory, not optional; additionally any lamports were transferred by the program, not pre-funded by an attacker), so no attacker-supplied prior state or size can exist

SOL-006.reachability: the privileged handler that mutates state without a Signer<> / is_signer check on the caller
exclusions: the AccountInfo is a documented `/// CHECK:` used only as a CPI target, program id, or read-only/sysvar ref — not a privileged caller whose signature matters
account.is_signer is asserted (or the field is a Signer<>/Account<>) before any state mutation
the account is never used to authorize a state change or fund movement — on-chain OR by an off-chain consumer of its emitted/logged key

SOL-007.reachability: the AccountInfo deserialize whose owner is never compared to program_id
exclusions: account.owner == program_id (or the expected program) is checked before deserializing
the account is an Anchor `Account<'info, T>` (Anchor enforces the owner) rather than a raw AccountInfo
the bytes are read only for display/logging and are never persisted, emitted in an event, or trusted for any authorization or fund decision — on-chain OR by an off-chain consumer of the emitted data

SOL-008.reachability: the use of a PDA account that is never re-derived and compared via find_program_address
exclusions: the address is re-derived via find_program_address and compared, or Anchor seeds = [...] + a canonical `bump` constraint enforce it (a `bump = <stored_field>` counts ONLY if that stored bump itself passed SOL-016 canonical-bump validation; has_one alone does NOT verify canonical PDA derivation and is not sufficient by itself; and if an Anchor `seeds::program = <id>` is used, that <id> must be a hardcoded/trusted program id, NOT an attacker-supplied or runtime-mutable value — including a field loaded from ANY account (even a typed Account<>) unless that field is a compile-time constant or was set by a verified admin and cannot be changed by non-admin callers)

SOL-009.reachability: the invoke_signed call and the missing upstream caller-authority check
exclusions: the caller's authority for THIS SPECIFIC privileged operation is verified (Signer + has_one/constraint binding the caller to the target resource) BEFORE the invoke_signed — a 'trusted target program' or any unrelated upstream Signer check is NOT sufficient

SOL-010.reachability: the reinit site — an init_if_needed account, OR a raw account-header write (.data.borrow_mut() / try_borrow_mut_data) — that holds value or authority (re-init drops/overwrites it)
exclusions: the account holds no lamports, token balances, authority keys, OR access-gating state that a second initialization could reset — access-gating state includes (non-exhaustively) a timestamp / nonce / status used as a lock, AND any field that controls subsequent PDA derivation, account creation, or role assignment

an explicit already-initialized guard REJECTS a second initialization before any write — for a hand-rolled `.data.borrow_mut()`/`try_borrow_mut_data` write the 8-byte discriminator is asserted all-zero (`data[0..8] == [0;8]`) or an `is_initialized`/version flag asserted false and the handler returns Err when already set (Orca `initialize_dynamic_tick_array`), for Anchor it is plain `init` / `#[account(zero)]`; a bare `.data.borrow_mut()` that only writes a data region of an already-type-validated account (discriminator/authority untouched) also clears this

the value-moving path is gated by a nullifier/spent-marker created with plain `init` so a duplicate redemption ABORTS AT ACCOUNT CREATION before any payout - NOT a mutable boolean flag in an existing account (a flag a reset/reinit path can re-open does NOT clear this rule)

SOL-011.reachability: the close= account that isn't fully drained/zeroed before close, or whose lamports go to an attacker-chosen destination
exclusions: the account is fully drained (lamports AND any token balances) before close and its data is zeroed, AND it holds no delegated authority over other on-chain resources (mints, PDAs, vaults) that must be explicitly revoked before close
the close destination is program-controlled or a signer-validated key, not an attacker-supplied account

SOL-012.reachability: the funded account used without a rent-exempt assertion
exclusions: the account is created with Anchor `init` (rent-exemption enforced by the framework)
a rent-exempt assertion (Rent::get) is present before/at funding

SOL-013.reachability: the hardcoded token-program id and the token account it is used to invoke
exclusions: the typed anchor_spl::token::ID / token_2022::ID is used via a typed Program<> account, not a raw literal

the literal lives only in a test/const and is NEVER reached on any runtime branch for a program id used in a CPI — including behind a #[cfg(feature = ...)] / #[cfg(not(test))] block that ships in ANY production build (verify the call site AND the build's enabled features, not just the declaration; only #[cfg(test)] truly excludes it)

SOL-014.reachability: the +/-/* on a balance/counter (attacker-influenced) without checked_*
exclusions: the operation already uses checked_/try_/saturating_ math with explicit error handling for the financial case
both operands are compile-time-bounded constants that cannot overflow/underflow

the value is non-financial AND does not feed any downstream financial calculation (proven by tracing every use-site, not a 'this field looks non-financial' claim), AND the operands are bounded so the maximum possible result cannot exceed the type's max (proven by an explicit checked bound or a type-level guarantee, not an unverified 'validated range')

SOL-015.reachability: the Account<'info, T> that cross-references another account with no has_one / constraint binding
exclusions: the related accounts are bound by has_one / constraint / seeds in the accounts struct
the relationship is enforced by an explicit require_keys_eq! in the handler body before use

SOL-016.reachability: a stored .bump whose init-site bump is not provably canonical — reused via `bump = <account>.bump` when init stored a caller-supplied bump, or read into a local and passed to create_program_address, with no find_program_address compare
exclusions: the read is `bump = <account>.bump` (or a bare `seeds = [...], bump` with NO `= target` after bump) on a typed `Account<'info, T>`, AND the SAME account's stored bump was written at init by Anchor's bare `bump` / `ctx.bumps.<name>` (canonical) — NOT a caller-supplied `#[instruction(bump)]` value and NOT a value from create_program_address: verify that exact init site, then dismiss (idiomatic canonical reuse, not a finding). If the init bump is caller-supplied or otherwise non-canonical, this reuse IS the bug — keep it (Anchor's `bump = <expr>` re-derives via create_program_address with the GIVEN bump, so a non-canonical stored bump still validates).
a non-constraint read is validated against the canonical bump before use (e.g. require!(stored == Pubkey::find_program_address(seeds, program_id).1))

the PDA (and its bump) is created in the same instruction using the canonical bump from find_program_address (NOT a caller-supplied bump passed to create_program_address, which accepts any valid off-curve bump and re-introduces the non-canonical-bump bug)

SOL-017.reachability: the raw data-buffer cast (&*account.data.borrow() / transmute) used without deserialize-then-validate
exclusions: a typed deserialize with length + discriminator validation precedes any field use
the cast is over a freshly-created, program-owned, length-checked buffer with a verified layout

SOL-018.reachability: the 32-ones System Program literal used instead of system_program::ID
exclusions: the program-id comparison uses the imported system_program::ID type-safely, not a raw string literal

the literal appears only in a #[cfg(test)] module or a const that is never reached on a runtime program-id verification — a #[cfg(feature = ...)] block that ships in a production build does NOT qualify

SOL-019.reachability: the try_deserialize_unchecked (or manual deserialize) that skips the 8-byte discriminator
exclusions: try_deserialize (with the discriminator check) is used, or the 8-byte discriminator is verified manually before the unchecked deserialize
the SAME account being deserialized is declared as an Anchor `Account<'info, T>` field (which enforces the discriminator) — not merely that some other account in the same handler is Anchor-typed

SOL-020.reachability: the SetAuthority CPI without a current-authority verification
exclusions: the current authority is verified to equal the expected key before the SetAuthority CPI

an Anchor `constraint = <signer>.key() == <resource>.authority` on a Signer<> (or has_one WHERE the bound authority field is itself declared Signer<>) binds the SIGNING caller to the CURRENT authority of the resource being changed — a bare Signer<> not bound to the stored authority key, OR a has_one/constraint on a NON-signing authority account (key matches but the holder never consents), is NOT sufficient

SOL-021.reachability: the close/resolve op guarded by a freshness/expiry condition that cannot hold once status is terminal
exclusions: a separate terminal-state release branch exists that ignores the freshness/expiry guard

the terminal-state value is unconditionally overwritten on EVERY termination path to a value that IRREVOCABLY satisfies the guard for all future time (e.g. i64::MAX / a permanent terminal flag — a transient value like now + grace_period that lets the guard fail again once the window elapses does NOT qualify), regardless of its prior (possibly attacker-set) value

SOL-022.reachability: the counter incremented when state degrades with no decrement / settlement path
exclusions: an inverse decrement / settlement path exists that clears the counter when the state recovers
the counter is monotonic AND verified to never gate resource reuse, fund release, OR any fee/penalty calculation (a code-path check tracing every use-site, not a 'by design' comment)

SOL-023.reachability: the fee/penalty integer division that rounds in the user's favor
exclusions: the amount the user OWES rounds up on the SHIPPED code path (div_ceil in the production build — a div_ceil behind ANY #[cfg(...)] attribute OR a `cfg!(...)` / const-bool branch condition (nightly, a feature flag, target_arch, etc.) while the shipped on-chain BPF build path divides with `/` does NOT qualify); only protocol-side payouts round down
a minimum-amount/dust floor is enforced so the rounding residual cannot be farmed

SOL-024.reachability: the oracle price read without a staleness (publish-slot age) or confidence check
exclusions: get_price_no_older_than (staleness, with a max-age bound that reflects the protocol's real staleness tolerance — u64::MAX or an unreasonably large age is NOT sufficient) AND a confidence-interval bound are both enforced before use

the price feeds a non-economic / display-only path that cannot trigger a trade, liquidation, or any other economic action — neither on-chain NOR via an off-chain consumer (e.g. a keeper reading emitted price events to trigger liquidations, rebalancing, or collateral updates)

SOL-025.reachability: the bincode::deserialize of a Clock/Rent sysvar instead of Clock::get() / Sysvar<>
exclusions: Clock::get() / Rent::get() or an Anchor Sysvar<> is used (the account key is checked internally)
the sysvar account key is explicitly verified against the canonical sysvar id before the raw deserialize

SOL-026.reachability: the two accounts that must differ but are never checked with require_keys_neq! (non-Anchor-Account paths)
exclusions: require_keys_neq! (or Anchor's duplicate-mutable Account<> rejection — which covers ONLY `Account<'info, T>`, NOT AccountLoader / UncheckedAccount / remaining_accounts) guards the pair
the two accounts are provably distinct by their seeds/constraints so the same key cannot be passed twice

SOL-027.reachability: the ctx.remaining_accounts element read/written/invoked without owner/key/signer validation
exclusions: each remaining account's owner/key/signer is validated before it is read, written, or invoked

remaining_accounts is iterated for display/logging only and no field is trusted for any authorization, fund-movement, or state-write decision — on-chain OR by an off-chain consumer of the logged/emitted data

SOL-028.reachability: the swap/withdraw/settle output derived with no caller min-out / max-in bound
exclusions: a caller-supplied min-out / max-in bound is taken and enforced before settlement

the output is fixed or oracle-bounded and not subject to an adverse swap/sandwich — and if oracle-bounded, the oracle itself enforces the SOL-024 staleness + confidence checks for ITS vendor (Pyth, Switchboard, etc.); a silent SOL-024 scanner result does NOT count (the scanner only catches the Pyth surface — verify the actual freshness check exists for whatever oracle is used), since a stale/wide oracle makes 'oracle-bounded' meaningless

SOL-029.reachability: the send path with skipPreflight: true (or no simulateTransaction before a mainnet send)
exclusions: preflight stays on, or simulateTransaction is called and err === null is asserted before the mainnet send

skipPreflight: true is on a devnet/test/throwaway path, not a value-moving mainnet send — AND the gate selecting it FAILS CLOSED (defaults to preflight ON for mainnet): an env check like `CLUSTER !== 'mainnet-beta'` that yields skipPreflight when the var is unset does NOT qualify; require an explicit non-mainnet allowlist
the priority fee is derived from getRecentPrioritizationFees() / a fee oracle and clamped to a sane max
microLamports: 0 (the intentional no-priority opt-out) or a documented test/config default

SOL-031.reachability: the Jupiter quote consumed (swap built) without a quoteResponse.contextSlot freshness check
exclusions: quoteResponse.contextSlot is captured and the route is refetched/rejected when it lags the current slot
the quote is consumed within the same slot as the fetch (an undefined 'freshness window' is not sufficient — prefer ex1's explicit contextSlot check) AND a slippage bound protects the fill

SOL-032.reachability: the amount/price computation applying a hardcoded decimals scale where a second mint (or a different-decimals mint) can enter the math
exclusions: decimals are read from the mint account (mint.decimals) and applied before any cross-mint comparison or division

a single mint is pinned by address in the program, the scale constant cites that mint, and no second mint can enter the math (an SPL mint's decimals are fixed at initializeMint and cannot change afterwards — but a CONFIGURABLE mint address with an assumed scale does NOT qualify)
the literal is not a token scale at all (compute-unit price, bps denominator, time constant) — name what it actually scales

SOL-033.reachability: the post-CPI read site and the CPI that can mutate the account it reads
exclusions: the account is reload()ed (or re-deserialized from its AccountInfo) between the CPI and the read

the callee provably cannot mutate the read account — it is not in the CPI's account set and the callee cannot reach it via nested CPI (name the callee and its full account set; 'the callee looks unrelated' is NOT sufficient)
the read value feeds only logs/events, never a gate, an amount computation, or stored state

SOL-034.reachability: the manual lamport write and the internal balance/claim field it must stay in sync with
exclusions: the mutation updates BOTH the lamports and the matching internal balance/claim field in the same instruction (cite both writes), and the debited account remains rent-exempt afterwards

the mutation is the documented rent-refund path of an account close: the destination is validated against stored state (not caller-chosen), and the account's data is zeroed or discarded in the same instruction

the accounts are system-owned and the movement uses a system-program transfer CPI — a manual write on a system-owned account cannot deduct anyway (the runtime rejects it); flag it as dead/misleading code

SOL-035.reachability: the instruction-introspection call site (load_instruction_at_checked / load_current_index_checked / get_instruction_relative) and the instructions-sysvar account it reads
exclusions: BOTH: the account read is an Anchor `Sysvar<'info, Instructions>` (or `account.key() == solana_program::sysvar::instructions::ID` is asserted), AND the introspected precompile instruction's program id, signer pubkey, AND signed message are all validated against the expected values before the result authorizes anything — pinning the sysvar alone is NOT sufficient (a real Ed25519/Secp256k1 ix over an attacker-chosen pubkey/message still passes a 'did a precompile run' check)

the introspection result is used only for logging/telemetry — never to authorize a state change, accept a precompile-verified signature, or gate a CPI-origin check (a positive 'not security-relevant' proof, not merely 'looks informational')

SOL-036.reachability: the token account trusted as a specific owner's ATA without a canonical-derivation check
exclusions: the account carries Anchor `associated_token::mint = <mint>` AND `associated_token::authority = <owner>` constraints (Anchor re-derives and enforces the canonical ATA)

the account key is compared against `get_associated_token_address(owner, mint)` (or the Token-2022 variant for the actual token program) before any deposit/payout, with owner and mint both sourced from validated on-chain state — NOT from caller-supplied instruction data
the token account is a program-owned vault pinned by a PDA seed/has_one (not a per-user ATA at all), so canonical-ATA derivation does not apply

SOL-037.reachability: the invoke/invoke_signed call site whose target program id is not pinned to an expected program
exclusions: the callee program is pinned (a typed Anchor `Program<'info, T>`, or its key asserted == the expected hardcoded/config-stored program id) AND the accounts passed into the CPI are validated/pinned — for an `invoke_signed` that carries this program's PDA authority, a pinned program with attacker-substituted accounts is still a confused-deputy drain (cite SOL-027 for the account validation)

the program id AND the account metas are all hardcoded constants / program-derived in the CPI call itself (not read from caller-supplied accounts or instruction data), so neither the callee nor its accounts can be redirected
this is SOL-009's concern (missing CALLER authority) rather than an unpinned CALLEE — cite SOL-009 instead; SOL-037 is specifically the callee-identity gap

SOL-038.reachability: cite the seeds = [...] expression (in #[account(seeds = ...)] or a find_program_address/create_program_address call) that places a variable-length, caller-influenced element (a String / Vec<u8> / &[u8] / unbounded slice) adjacent to another variable-length element or directly after a non-fixed-width literal, with no fixed-width per-type discriminator separating them — OR a second seed scheme in the same program that ends in a variable element and whose fixed prefix differs in length from a sibling's (so the two flatten to the same bytes) — together with a create/init or address-keyed lookup that trusts the resulting PDA as a unique per-entity address.
exclusions: The seed array has at most ONE variable-length element and it is the LAST element, every element before it is fixed-width (a fixed-length namespace literal like b"vault", a Pubkey's 32 bytes, a u8/u64::to_le_bytes(), or a [u8; N]) — AND one of the following holds so cross-scheme aliasing is also excluded: (a) this is the program's ONLY PDA scheme that ends in a variable-length element, OR (b) every same-namespace scheme that ends in a variable element carries a fixed-width leading per-type discriminator drawn from one program-wide registry (see exclusion 4), OR (c) all sibling schemes' fixed prefixes are provably equal-length. A single trailing variable prevents only INTRA-scheme byte-shifting; it does NOT prevent two trailing-variable schemes with unequal-length fixed prefixes from aliasing — e.g. [b"a", name] and [b"ab", name2] collide on a|bX == ab|X. Without (a), (b), or (c), do NOT suppress.

Every variable-length element is normalized to a FIXED width before being placed in the seeds — hashed to 32 bytes (e.g. hash(name).to_bytes() / keccak), length-prefixed with its own byte count, or truncated/padded to a constant [u8; N] — so element boundaries are unambiguous regardless of content. (Width-fixing alone clears the intra-scheme shift; if more than one record type shares this layout it must ALSO carry the exclusion-4 discriminator, since equal-width-but-untagged schemes still cross-alias.)

The seed material is entirely fixed-width or program-controlled (only Pubkeys, fixed integer encodings, enum discriminants, or hardcoded equal-length literals) with NO caller-supplied variable-length bytes, so an attacker cannot shift any boundary or pick a colliding value.

Every same-namespace scheme leads with a fixed-width per-type discriminator (seed[0]) drawn from a SINGLE program-wide enum/registry whose variants are guaranteed distinct AND a CONSISTENT fixed width across the registry (e.g. #[repr(u32)] enum PdaTag { ... } used as PdaTag::X as u32, never a 1-byte tag that could equal a literal seed prefix and never mixed widths since a narrower tag can prefix a wider one) AND no remaining element can byte-shift against the next (each is fixed-width or the variable element is last and width-fixed per exclusion 2). A discriminator that is a free-floating per-file const with no registry does NOT qualify — nothing prevents two account types from sharing the same value and re-colliding.

A fixed-width element (a 32-byte Pubkey via key().as_ref(), a [u8; N], a fixed integer encoding, or a hashed/length-prefixed element) placed BETWEEN two variable-length seeds pins both boundaries independently -- no byte can shift across a fixed separator (matching it would require the variable bytes to reproduce the exact fixed value at a shifted offset, infeasible for a non-degenerate value) -- so two variable seeds separated by a Pubkey or other fixed-width element are SAFE. The regex correctly does not fire on this (only directly-adjacent .as_bytes(), .as_bytes() triggers it); a reviewer applying exclusion 1 should likewise treat any two variables separated by a fixed-width element as cleared.

SOL-039.reachability: the inner fund-moving CPI call site whose Result is discarded (let _ =, .ok(), .is_err()/.is_ok() logged-and-ignored, .unwrap_or*, or a match/if-let-Err arm that does not re-?) inside a handler that has already written one of its own program-owned accounts before that CPI
exclusions: The swallowed call is not a fund-moving CPI — a local helper, msg!, or checked-arith Result with no external/cross-account effect. Confirm the discarded Result belongs to an invoke/invoke_signed or token:: CPI, not an unrelated value.

The CPI is actually `?`-propagated or `.map_err(..)?`'d — the instruction reverts on failure, so there is no asymmetry. (The regex does not fire on a bare `?`/`.map_err(..)?` call; cite this only if a reviewer mis-reads a propagated call.) This also covers a `match`/`if let Err(e) =` whose arm `return Err(e)`s or `?`-propagates - the instruction still reverts, so there is no asymmetry even though the regex fires on the `match`/`if let` head.

The discarded Result feeds a `require!` / `assert!` / `ensure!` (e.g. `require!(token::transfer(..).is_ok(), E)`): this RETURNS Err on failure and reverts the whole instruction, so it is SAFE. The regex FIRES on every `require!`/`assert!`/`ensure!`-guarded `.is_ok()` (it is lookbehind-free / RE2-compatible) - cite this exclusion to dismiss them; they are safe because the macro returns Err on failure and reverts the instruction.

The catch branch (`.ok()` consequence, the `Err(..)` match arm, the `if let Err` body) FULLY rolls back every prior self-mutation before returning — re-credits the debt, un-burns the shares, restores the nonce — so committed state stays symmetric on failure.

No program-owned account is written before AND the swallow leaves no attacker-controllable asymmetry — i.e. the CPI is the handler's only state change, OR the only prior writes are idempotent set-to-constant values that a replay/retry re-derives identically (nothing the attacker can farm by forcing the CPI to fail). NOTE: cite this even when an UNRELATED write follows the CPI later in the handler — the gate is 'was a dependent self-mutation committed before the swallow that a failed CPI would orphan', not 'is the CPI the literal last statement'.

SOL-040.reachability: the deposit/mint-shares handler that credits an internal balance/share field from the requested transfer `amount` (or an instruction-data amount field) rather than from a measured pre/post balance delta of the program's destination token account — AND/OR a deposit handler whose destination token account or accounting mint is not pinned to the vault's program-controlled authority, so an honest delta measures an attacker-substituted account or a worthless attacker-minted asset
exclusions: the credited amount is computed from a measured pre/post delta — the destination token account is reload()ed and its `.amount` read both immediately BEFORE and immediately AFTER the transfer CPI, and the credit is `post.checked_sub(pre)` (not the `amount` argument); a single post-transfer read without a captured pre-balance is NOT sufficient when the account can hold a prior balance

BINDING (mandatory in addition to the measured delta — a measured delta alone does NOT clear this rule): the destination token account is pinned to a program-controlled authority and the mint is pinned/validated against the vault's accounting asset, with both constraints VISIBLE IN THE ACCOUNTS STRUCT — e.g. `#[account(mut, associated_token::mint = mint, associated_token::authority = vault)]` (or seeds-derived `token::authority = <vault pda>` + `token::mint = mint`) on the destination account, plus `has_one = mint` on the vault (or a pinned mint address); if the destination `vault_ata` is a bare `InterfaceAccount<'info, TokenAccount>` with no authority/mint binding, or the `mint` is unconstrained, the handler is STILL drainable via wrong-account substitution or worthless-mint deposit even when the delta math is correct — do NOT clear it on the strength of the delta

the deposit mint is pinned by address to a plain SPL Token mint (token program == anchor_spl::token::ID, not token_2022::ID) OR the handler asserts the Token-2022 mint carries NO TransferFee AND NO TransferHook extension (e.g. via get_extension::<TransferFeeConfig>()/<TransferHook>() returning none — checking extension PRESENCE, fixed at init, not the current fee rate) before crediting — so the received amount provably equals the requested amount; 'we only support standard tokens' without a pin or an extension check is NOT sufficient. (This clears the under-crediting threat only; the BINDING exclusion above still applies independently.)

the value moved is a fixed, program-controlled internal transfer where the destination token account's authority is a program-owned PDA visible in the accounts struct AND the mint is pinned, so no external mint with fee/hook semantics can be substituted and no foreign token account can be passed — a positive, in-struct 'no fee path and no substitution can apply here' proof, not a prose 'this looks internal' assertion

the `amount` is used only to bound/validate the transfer (e.g. a max-in cap) and is never the source of the credited share/balance figure — the credit is sourced from the measured delta — AND the binding exclusion above is independently satisfied

SOL-041.reachability: the price/share/payout computation that reads a raw vault `lamports()` or token-account `amount` (or the absolute post-CPI balance) as the supply/reserve total, plus the permissionless balance-inflation path — a plain SPL/SystemProgram transfer into that vault, a Token-2022 fee/interest credit, OR a pre-existing balance seeded before the instruction runs (front-run init / prior-slot transfer / rent top-up) — that lets an attacker move the "total" without a matching ledger write
exclusions: the supply/reserve total driving the calculation is a program-owned stored ledger field (e.g. `state.recorded_reserve` / `state.recorded_shares`) that is mutated ONLY inside accounted deposit/withdraw/skim handlers by a MEASURED balance-delta (snapshot before, `reload()` after the CPI per SOL-033, credit `after − before` with `checked_*` per SOL-014 — never the requested `amount_in`), and the live `lamports()` / token `amount` is read for at most a solvency assertion (e.g. require live >= recorded), never as the value fed into the price/share/payout math

the raw balance is read only to GATE solvency (require `vault.amount >= owed`) or for display/logging, and is provably never used as a divisor, multiplier, or supply input to mint shares / set a price / size a payout (trace every use-site to a concrete non-pricing sink — a 'looks like a balance check' claim is not sufficient)

the vault is a per-trade escrow whose entire balance is created and consumed within ONE instruction by the program itself AND the read uses the in-instruction balance-DELTA it credited (snapshot-before / `reload()` / `after − before`), NOT the absolute `vault.amount` — on Solana a vault/escrow PDA can be pre-funded by anyone before the instruction ever executes (front-run init, prior-slot transfer, rent top-up), so an absolute-balance read is NOT made safe merely by being single-instruction

a donated surplus is reconciled only by an admin-gated skim instruction that the caller must SIGN AND that is bound by constraint to a hardcoded/program-stored admin key, that updates `recorded_reserve` (and `recorded_shares` if applicable) atomically with the tokens it moves so the solvency invariant still holds afterward, and the share/price math still derives from the stored ledger rather than the post-skim live balance

the pool is protected against first-depositor inflation independently of this read — minimum-liquidity dead shares are locked on seed (or a virtual-reserve/virtual-share offset is used) AND dust deposits that round to zero shares are rejected (`require!(shares > 0)`) — so even a handler that later moves reserve independently of shares cannot be gamed into a 1-share pool

SOL-042.reachability: the loop/iterator whose trip count is bound to an attacker-influenced length (ctx.remaining_accounts.len(), a Vec/map field a user can grow, or an append-only/admin-grown global list) with no per-instruction cap enforced before it. The regex matches both single-var and tuple-binding `for` loops (`for acc in …` and `for (i, acc) in remaining_accounts.iter().enumerate()`); it still misses non-`for` shapes: `while i < …len()` index loops and `.iter().for_each/map/fold(…)` chains
exclusions: the iteration is bounded by an enforced per-instruction cap BEFORE the loop (require!(list.len() <= MAX) / a fixed-size slice / .take(MAX) over a *validated* length / a `[T; N]` array) where MAX is a constant proven to fit the CU budget for this loop body — NOT an unverified 'it's usually small' assumption. HUMAN-VERIFY (RE2 cannot see this): the cap must not be a `.take()`/truncating slice that silently DROPS unprocessed entries when correctness requires all of them (e.g. a settlement/payout set) — that is a correctness bug masquerading as a fix; paginate instead. A truncating cap only qualifies when dropping the tail is provably correct for this handler.

the collection is append-only or growable but its GROWTH path is itself capped so it can never exceed the executable CU bound — a bounded `Vec`/`require!` at *every* push/realloc site, with the cited push site actually shown to be bounded. HUMAN-VERIFY (machine cannot prove a negative across the codebase): 'growth is probably bounded somewhere' is NOT a dismissal — name the file+line of the push site and show the cap there. A cap on the read/loop while the stored list can still grow unbounded does NOT qualify (a near-max list plus one more entry can still tip a *different* reader over).

the loop length is fixed by program state that can NEVER exceed the executable CU bound — a compile-time constant, a `[T; N]` array, or a count derived from validated PDAs the program itself created under a bounded scheme. NOTE: 'only an admin/Signer can grow it' does NOT by itself qualify — an admin (or a compromised/buggy admin path) that grows an append-only list past the CU bound bricks the instruction for everyone; the test is 'length is bounded by a CU-provable cap', not 'an attacker can't influence the length'. Prove the bound by tracing every write site, not 'this list looks internal'.

work is explicitly paginated / chunked across transactions with a persisted cursor (or an offset+limit argument) so no single instruction processes more than a bounded slice, the cursor cannot be reset to replay or skip work, AND — when the loop credits/pays/settles accounts — each iterated account is bound by identity to authoritative program state at the cursor offset (require_keys_eq! against a stored registry/PDA per index), so the cursor SELECTS recipients rather than merely counting iterations. A count cap + bare cursor that pays whatever the caller passes does NOT qualify — that is a double-pay/skip fund-drain (SOL-027), strictly worse than the DoS, and is NOT excluded by this rule.

SOL-043.reachability: the permissionless instruction handler that (a) appends a caller-controlled entry to a persistent shared account / grows it via realloc/init_if_needed with no cap, (b) gates registration behind a shared monotonic counter that only increments and is never decremented on close, or (c) closes / front-runs the init of a singleton PDA other instructions depend on — with no per-caller scoping, no caller-funded rent, no slot-release/deposit, and no admin gate
exclusions: per-caller data lives in ONE fixed-size PDA seeded by the principal's own key (seeds = [..., caller.key().as_ref()], one account per caller, no shared growable list) AND rent is paid by that caller (payer = caller) — so a single attacker can inflate only their own rent-paid account and cannot enlarge shared state or evict others. This is the preferred shape; a shared global cap is NOT required when each caller is isolated this way.

where a SHARED cap is used, it is genuinely self-limiting: the slot count is DECREMENTED in a close/deregister handler so closing an entry frees a slot, AND/OR each registration requires a refundable deposit/stake that makes N throwaway-key Sybils economically prohibitive. A monotonic `require!(count < MAX_ENTRIES)` over a counter that only ever increments (never decremented on close) is NOT sufficient — that is itself a permissionless global-exhaustion DoS (the SOL-022 write-only-counter pattern) and does NOT clear this rule, even though total size is bounded; 'size bounded' is not 'service available'.

each appended slot's incremental rent is paid by the CALLER themselves (payer = caller, or a system-program transfer in the SAME instruction) — growth is self-limiting and the program/treasury never subsidizes it; a program-funded or PDA-funded grow (realloc::payer = vault/program) is NOT sufficient.

the close / lifecycle-transition of the depended-on PDA is gated by a Signer<> bound by constraint to a hardcoded or program-stored admin/authority key (close = admin with has_one = admin WHERE admin is declared Signer<>, or constraint = signer.key() == config.admin) — a bare Signer<> the caller self-assigns, a has_one on a NON-signer account, or a `close` reachable by any caller, is NOT sufficient.

the singleton PDA exposed to an init-front-run is seeded by a FIXED or admin-controlled key (not caller-supplied data), is created at deploy time, OR its init is idempotent (re-init is a no-op / verifies the existing state belongs to the program) — so an attacker cannot pre-create it with hostile state or block legitimate creation. A permissionless `init`/`init_if_needed` of a depended-on singleton whose seeds an attacker can satisfy first is NOT sufficient.

SOL-044.reachability: the accrual/rate computation (interest, emissions, vesting, funding) that converts a slot count or slot delta to elapsed time via a hardcoded slots-per-period or ms-per-slot constant instead of reading Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp
exclusions: the elapsed time driving the accrual is computed from Clock::get()?.unix_timestamp deltas (e.g. now_ts - last_update_ts on stored i64 timestamps), and the slots-per-period / ms-per-slot constant is used only for a non-economic, non-priority purpose such as log formatting or a UI hint that never scales a payout and never decides ordering/fill/liquidation/seniority — naming which it is

the hardcoded constant is NOT a slot→time conversion at all — name what it actually is (a compute-unit budget, a bps/percentage denominator, a fixed-point Q-scale, a seeds/byte-length constant, or a per-slot reward that is intentionally denominated in slots by spec with the slot-denomination cited) — so no wall-clock assumption is embedded

the protocol is provably slot-denominated by design: cite the spec clause that defines the rate per SLOT rather than per unit of real time, AND trace every consumer of the slot-accrued field to confirm none compares, sums, or mixes it with a unix_timestamp-derived value (any such mix reintroduces the drift; this is an explicit trace of all readers, not a glance)

the slot delta is converted to time only to form an UPPER/LOWER bound in a conservative safety check, AND the citer states (a) the comparison sign and (b) the worst-case drift direction (slots historically run SLOWER than 400ms → the same slot delta spans MORE wall-clock), and shows that under that drift the check can only ever REJECT more than wall-clock would (stricter), never ACCEPT more value than real time allows — a max-staleness gate `now_slot - last_slot < MAX` is NOT covered, because slow slots make it accept quotes that are actually staler than intended

SOL-045.reachability: the append / set_leaf / replace_leaf (or hand-rolled compute_root over filled_subtrees / changelog) call site that updates the stored root, AND the verify_leaf / proof-check instruction that later validates a proof against that root — exploitability is confirmed when a proof for a never-inserted leaf rehashes to the stored root, or an inserted leaf's proof fails against it. Both sites must be cited: a correct mutation paired with a verify path that trusts a caller-supplied or stale root is still exploitable, and a correct verify paired with a divergent incremental root is still exploitable
exclusions: ALL root maintenance AND all proof verification are delegated to the audited spl-account-compression program via CPI (append / replace_leaf / verify_leaf) and the handler only marshals accounts — delegating only the mutation (append/replace_leaf) while hand-rolling or trusting a caller-supplied root in the proof-verifying instruction does NOT clear the finding (the verify path is half the vuln class). The merkle_tree account passed into the CPI must additionally be pinned to spl_account_compression::ID via an Anchor `owner = …` constraint or a runtime require_keys_eq! on merkle_tree.owner (UncheckedAccount + has_one does NOT bind the tree authority — the account is never deserialized). A local copy/fork of the crate that has been MODIFIED does NOT qualify and must be re-audited.

FOR A HAND-ROLLED TREE, the following three conditions must ALL hold together (they are conjunctive, not independent OR-satisfiers; clearing on any one alone leaves the other half of the class open): (a) a differential test proves the incremental root equals a full bottom-up recomputation over RANDOMIZED insert AND replace sequences spanning multiple tree depths, the buffer-wraparound boundary, AND out-of-order / concurrent changelog consumption (the distinguishing failure mode of a ConcurrentMerkleTree vs a plain one — a test that only does sequential append/replace can pass while the concurrency path stays broken); a single happy-path append or a fixed hardcoded-sequence test is NOT sufficient — cite the test; AND (b) the empty/default node hash used at each level is the protocol-fixed constant identical to the one the full recompute uses, AND leaf-index path direction is derived from the canonical bit decomposition of the index (not an unverified 'sibling on the left/right' assumption), both verified against the recompute rather than a 'looks symmetric' read; AND (c) every proof-verifying instruction rehashes the supplied proof up to and compares against the STORED on-chain root using the leaf index's path direction — NOT a caller-supplied root, a cached/changelog root that may be stale, or a root read from an unvalidated account.

the instruction is read-only with respect to the tree (no append/set_leaf/replace_leaf/compute_root mutation site AND no proof-verifying/inclusion-check site is present in the reviewed path) — the divergence class requires at least one of the two sites to be reachable, so a handler that neither mutates the root nor verifies a proof against it is out of scope

SOL-046.reachability: the native entrypoint / hand-rolled dispatcher (match on instruction_data[0] or a split-first tag byte) that routes to a handler taking a bare &[AccountInfo] slice, where the routed handler then reads/mutates an account without re-deriving the discriminator, owner, PDA (canonical-bump compare), or signer that Anchor's #[derive(Accounts)] would have enforced
exclusions: the dispatched handler is an Anchor `#[derive(Accounts)]` context (the accounts arrive as a typed `Context<T>` whose struct carries the relevant `Account<'info,_>` / `Signer<>` / `has_one` / `seeds`+`bump` / `owner` constraints) — i.e. the hand-rolled `match` only selects an Anchor handler and does NOT itself consume a raw `&[AccountInfo]`; Anchor's generated guards still run

this IS a deliberate native (non-Anchor) program AND every account on the matched arm is manually re-validated before use — a positive 'all four guards present on THIS arm' proof, not 'the program looks careful': (a) the 8-byte discriminator is verified via `try_deserialize` (NOT `try_deserialize_unchecked`) or an explicit constant-tag compare; (b) `owner == program_id` (or the expected program) is asserted on each account whose data is trusted; (c) each claimed PDA is re-derived via `find_program_address` and the returned CANONICAL bump is compared against the account's STORED bump (SOL-016) — re-derivation via `create_program_address` with a CALLER-SUPPLIED bump does NOT count, because it accepts any valid off-curve bump and re-introduces the non-canonical-bump bug; and (d) `is_signer` is checked on every privileged/authority account

the byte-match is not an instruction dispatcher at all — it is a bounded enum/version-tag parse on already-program-owned, discriminator-validated data (e.g. matching a state-machine status byte read out of an `Account<'info,T>` whose owner and discriminator Anchor already checked), so no account validation is being skipped

the matched first byte selects only among handlers that take ZERO accounts (pure compute / read-only view that returns data WITHOUT reading, writing, moving lamports from, or CPI-ing through any passed account) — so there is no account whose owner/signer/PDA/discriminator could be forged. NOTE: a 'view' that READS even one passed account is NOT covered — it must still validate that account's owner and discriminator before trusting the data it returns

SOL-047.reachability: the redeem/burn/claim handler that reads a caller-supplied receipt Mint or share token account and pays out the underlying asset (CPI transfer / lamport credit) without that mint being asserted == the vault-stored receipt mint AND the burned token account bound to it; the cited call-site must show an attacker-substitutable mint/share-account reaching the burn or payout, not merely an unpinned Mint arg in an init/mint-authority context
exclusions: The receipt mint is pinned to the deposit-produced mint stored in program state -- Anchor `address = <vault>.receipt_mint` or an explicit `require_keys_eq!(receipt_mint.key(), vault.receipt_mint)` before any burn or payout -- AND the burned share token account carries `token::mint = receipt_mint` (or its `.mint` is asserted == that pinned mint). BOTH bindings are required: pinning only the Mint arg while the share token account's mint is unchecked (or vice-versa) is still exploitable and is NOT cleared by this exclusion -- it is the incomplete-fix variant.

The share token account is a typed Anchor `Account<'info, TokenAccount>` whose `token::mint` / `associated_token::mint` is constrained to a mint that is itself program-derived or stored-in-state (not a caller-passed Mint), so the (mint, balance) pair cannot be forged. NOTE: this clears only the forgery/identity concern; it says nothing about whether the redeemed AMOUNT is then computed safely -- a perfectly pinned mint can still over-pay via a bad exchange rate or unbounded amount. That residual is the share-accounting class (out of scope for SOL-047); clear the SOL-047 identity finding here, but do not infer the redeem path is fully safe.

This is a one-mint protocol where the receipt mint is a hardcoded constant, or a fixed PDA `seeds = [b"receipt", vault.key().as_ref()]` re-derived in the same instruction (not read from a caller account), AND that canonical mint's `mint_authority` is the program/vault PDA (verified at init) so supply cannot be inflated by an external authority. A fixed/pinned mint *pubkey* whose mint authority is an outside key does NOT qualify -- the attacker mints unlimited genuine receipt tokens against a real mint, which is still SOL-047.

The redeemed amount is computed solely from program-stored per-user accounting (a position/receipt PDA owned by this program and bound by has_one/seeds to the caller) and the receipt mint/share token account is used only as an identity tag that is itself pinned per exclusion #1 -- the payout reads the recorded position, never a caller-supplied token balance or a caller-supplied amount. (If instead the handler pays out a caller-passed `shares`/`amount` arg or a caller-supplied token balance, this exclusion does NOT apply -- that is the unbounded-amount design exclusion #2 warns about, separate from the identity bug but not cleared here.)

SOL-048.reachability: the authorization/membership gate (require_keys_eq! / require! / a manual `==` against a stored field) whose compared field has an all-zero default AND is reachable before that field is provably set to a non-default value on a canonical (PDA/singleton/address-bound) account — OR whose host account is attacker-substitutable (no seeds/has_one/address binding), so an attacker can supply their own config with the field set to a value they control
exclusions: the gate compares against a field that is provably non-zero on a CANONICAL account before the comparison: (a) the host config/root account is bound by `seeds`/`bump`, `has_one`, or an explicit address check so it cannot be attacker-substituted, AND (b) an explicit `bool is_initialized` (or status enum) is asserted true, AND (c) the field was written in a verified-admin instruction to a value checked `!= the type's zero sentinel` at write time (`Pubkey::default()` for a Pubkey, `[0u8;32]` for a 32-byte root, `0` for a discriminator/nonce). A bare Anchor discriminator alone is NOT sufficient (it proves the account was created, not that THIS field was populated), and is_initialized==true on an UNBOUND account is NOT sufficient (Bring-Your-Own-Config still defeats the gate) — all three of (a),(b),(c) are required

the stored value being compared is a canonical hardcoded constant or a compile-time program id (never the zeroed default of a runtime-mutable account field), so no uninitialized or attacker-supplied state can ever reach the comparison

the zero/default value is explicitly rejected at the gate before any trust decision (`require_keys_neq!(stored, Pubkey::default())`, `require!(root != [0u8;32], ...)`, `require!(nonce != 0, ...)`, or a zero-sentinel routed exclusively to an UNAUTHORIZED/reject branch — a positive 'zero is denied' proof, not 'the default is probably never hit') AND the host account is canonical/bound (else the attacker just supplies a non-zero root on their own config)

the field is a pure non-security value (display label, free-form metadata) that never gates authorization, membership, fund movement, OR PDA/account derivation — proven by tracing every use-site, not 'this field looks cosmetic'. NOTE: a field consumed in PDA seed derivation IS a security input even if it reads as cosmetic (a metadata/label field reused as a seed is a trust input that selects which account/authority the gate resolves to), so this exclusion does NOT apply to any field that ever appears in a `seeds = [...]`

SOL-049.reachability: a hand-rolled zero-copy load site — bytemuck::from_bytes / try_from_bytes / cast_ref over a buffer, a manual transmute or *const T cast over data.borrow(), a hand-written `unsafe impl Pod`, or a raw `[u8; N]` byte indexed directly — where a flag byte is branched on without a canonical-value check OR an alignment/padding byte flows into a hash/equality/serialization, AND a writable code path that lets the attacker set that byte. The safe `#[account(zero_copy)]`+derived-Pod path with a bool field does not compile and is NOT reachable.
exclusions: the flag is a u8 (not a bool) AND every read path asserts canonicality before use — require!(flag <= 1) (or a match that rejects all bytes except the enumerated valid ones) runs on EVERY load, not only at init — AND the branch tests an exact value (flag == 1), never flag != 0

the struct uses Anchor's #[account(zero_copy)] (or derives bytemuck::Pod/Zeroable via the real derive macro — NOT a hand-written `unsafe impl Pod`) on a layout with NO bool fields and NO implicit padding: every byte is a named field, reserved/padding fields included, and those reserved bytes are zero-checked on load — so there is no type-system-skipped byte for an attacker to set and no UB-bool path

no padding/reserved byte and no aliased/union field is ever observable: the reinterpreted value is used field-by-field only, and no whole-struct bytes are hashed, equality-compared, serialized, or re-borrowed through an overlapping view (this disqualifies the hand-impl-Pod padding-leak trap that survives a clean u8 flag)

the account holding the buffer is provably never attacker-writable for this byte: it is program-owned and only ever written by handlers gated to a signer bound by constraint to a hardcoded/program-stored admin key (a bare Signer<> the caller self-assigns is NOT sufficient), and the buffer is not a caller-supplied AccountInfo reinterpreted with this layout (that is the SOL-017/SOL-007 trap)
the value is provably discarded — never used in an authority/state gate, written back, hashed, or emitted (a positive 'not security-relevant' proof, not merely 'this handler does not seem to use it')

SOL-050.reachability: the read/deserialize site whose field widths, field order, or byte offsets disagree with the write/serialize site for the same account (the loaded value differs from what was stored), including a second hand-written reader (`from_le_bytes` / manual offset) that parallels — and drifts from — a typed write, or two programs that each use their OWN copy of a "same" type that has diverged
exclusions: BOTH the write and read side go through ONE shared (de)serializer over the SAME type DEFINITION (same struct in the same crate/version, not just "a derived codec on each side") — one Anchor `#[account]` type, one `#[derive(BorshSerialize, BorshDeserialize)]` struct, or one `#[repr(C)]` `bytemuck::Pod` struct loaded via `AccountLoader` on BOTH sides — with NO hand-written byte slicing / `from_le_bytes` / manual offset on either side. A duplicated type copied into a second program/module that may have drifted does NOT qualify: the two definitions must be the literal same source (shared crate dependency), because two independently-edited "Vault" types each using their own derive can still disagree on width/order.

the layout is a zero-copy / Pod struct that is `#[repr(C)]` (or `#[repr(C, packed)]`) AND is loaded through that one Pod type via `AccountLoader` on BOTH the write and read side (symmetric by construction). A `const_assert_eq!(size_of::<T>(), N)` is REQUIRED additionally as a width/field-count tripwire, but is NOT sufficient on its own to dismiss a flag: `size_of` is a single scalar, so a same-size field REORDER passes the assertion unchanged. A bare `#[derive(Pod)]` on a default `#[repr(Rust)]` struct (compiler may reorder) also does NOT qualify.

both the write and read go through one manual offset/width defined ONCE as shared named constants (`const BAL_OFF`, `const BAL_LEN`) referenced by both sides AND covered by a round-trip property test that asserts `unpack(pack(x)) == x` over the field's full range — a single happy-path encode/decode is NOT sufficient.

the disagreeing value is a temporary that is decoded and fully consumed WITHIN the same function (never stored back to an account, returned, emitted, or read by any later authority/accounting gate) — a locally-scoped, locally-checkable non-persistence, NOT a whole-program "never used downstream" claim (which is not verifiable at a single write/read site and should not be asserted).

SOL-051.reachability: the instruction that selects a winner / rolls a trait / picks an ordering and reads Clock unix_timestamp/slot, the RecentBlockhashes or SlotHashes sysvar, or another pre-tx-observable value as the seed, then writes a value-bearing result (payout, mint, rank) from it — confirm the modulo/reduction result is read by the value-bearing decision, not by a cooldown/rate-limit/epoch-index path
exclusions: the randomness comes from a VRF whose ORACLE-OWNED result account is verified before use — you assert `*acct.owner == <switchboard/orao program id>` (or use the oracle's typed wrapper that enforces it) AND parse it with the oracle's type (e.g. Switchboard `RandomnessAccountData::parse`), AND that result account is bound to THIS specific draw by a key recorded at request/commit time (`has_one`, or comparison against a `Pubkey` stored in your state) — a VRF whose result account is read but never owner-checked, OR bound only via a `seeds=[…, pool.key()]` PDA re-derived under YOUR program id (which can never point at a genuine oracle account and is itself attacker-writable), is NOT sufficient

the value is read through the oracle's reveal method that FAILS when the round is not yet fulfilled (e.g. `RandomnessAccountData::get_value(clock.slot)` returning `RandomnessNotResolved`) and a zeroed/unrevealed buffer is rejected — a self-set `fulfilled`/`settled` bool on a program-local account, or reading the buffer before fulfillment, does NOT qualify, AND the request is fresh (the committed `seed_slot`/commit slot is checked so a stale or expired round cannot be replayed)

the draw uses a commit–reveal where the committed value is stored on-chain BEFORE the seed material becomes knowable and the reveal is checked against the commitment (hash preimage) — a 'commit' that commits to a value the committer can still grind at reveal time does NOT qualify

the timestamp/slot feeds time-bucketing, a cooldown or rate-limit window, or expiry math (`now % period`, `slot % epoch_len` as an epoch/round index), NOT a value-bearing draw outcome — proven by tracing that no payout, mint, rank, or fund-routing decision reads the modulo result (this is the single most common legitimate use of `unix_timestamp %` / `slot % len` and is the primary false-positive class on the timestamp/slot regex arms)

the on-chain value (timestamp/slot/blockhash/key) feeds a NON-value-bearing, non-adversarial use only — a UI tiebreaker, a non-prize display shuffle, or jitter on a value no party profits from steering — proven by tracing that no payout, mint, rank, or fund-routing decision reads the result (a positive 'no value rides on this draw' proof, not 'looks cosmetic')
the value is used as a uniqueness/nonce or PDA seed, NOT as the random outcome itself (predictability is fine for a nonce; the draw result must not be a function of it)

SOL-052.reachability: the token-handling path that accepts a generic InterfaceAccount / possibly-Token-2022 mint and assumes classic SPL behavior - crediting the requested (not received) amount, or moving value without checking for TransferFee / TransferHook / NonTransferable / DefaultAccountState(Frozen) / PermanentDelegate extensions
exclusions: the program is hardwired to classic SPL Token via a typed Program<'info, Token> (anchor_spl::token::ID) on EVERY token CPI (not just the deposit path) AND the mint is constrained so a Token-2022 mint can never enter the handler - Token-2022 extensions cannot apply to a mint the classic Token program owns

the mint's extensions are explicitly enumerated via StateWithExtensions / get_extension_types() and every UNSUPPORTED one is REJECTED before any value moves - TransferHook, NonTransferable, DefaultAccountState(Frozen), PermanentDelegate - and TransferFeeConfig is HANDLED via a payer-side measured delta (NOT merely absent from the reject set); a Program<Token2022> pin or a 'we only list vanilla mints' comment is NOT sufficient, and account-level extensions on the touched ATAs (CpiGuard, TransferFeeAmount) are inspected too

the received amount is the PAYER-side measured delta (the user's source ATA before-minus-after, or a fresh per-deposit escrow ATA no other party can pay into), so a transfer-fee skim cannot over-credit, AND the destination token account is bound to the vault by Anchor constraints (token::mint + token::authority) so a substituted or worthless-mint account cannot be passed

the token only ever leaves the program (one-way payout to a user-chosen account) and is never re-credited to internal accounting nor used to mint shares, so a fee skim or transfer-hook cannot create an internal-vs-actual imbalance
